races.name: Bath Country Race Day, What A Way To Make Weekend! EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anna Belardo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by Richard Newland & Jamie Insole whose T14 strike rate of 0/13 tempers connections' form but whose ability to get a solo lead here is the dominant tactical fact; Good ground suits (2/3 in similar conditions), though 104 days off is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Etienne
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly arrives with the highest realistic OR in the field at 86 and a placed effort over C&D conditions to her name; she travels prominently, which is precisely the position to be in behind an uncontested leader on this track, and Saffie Osborne's experience is a positive.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with five runs of recent placed form over this exact 5f-5½f trip on Good ground (3P from 5 similar-going runs), making J S Moore's charge interesting for the late stages; the 2-day turnaround is aggressive and a 7lb claim from Isobelle Chalmers helps offset the OR gulf.

runners_data.name: Tree Wizard
runners_data.note: Genuine front-running type by nature with three placing efforts from five runs on Good ground, but with prominent slots already occupied by Anna Belardo and Etienne, this horse is likely to race further back than ideal — the 0.92 STYLE_FIT flag tempers enthusiasm for scenarios that require it to reproduce its best from a held-up position.

runners_data.name: Cotai Jaunt
runners_data.note: Lightly raced debutante for Ollie Sangster (T14: 3/30, a warm stable in form) who showed little in a Stanmore maiden on debut over 6f; Sean Bowen takes the ride and brings strong tactical awareness, but with only one run to go on and unknown form in this company, her profile is uncertain.

runners_data.name: Polly The Sniper
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's filly has run twice, finishing fifth and sixth on debut efforts at distances slightly longer than today's 5½f; she holds a prominent style and the drop to this trip and Good ground could see a slightly sharper performance, though the OR of 120 reflects raw potential rather than achieved form.

races.paceDynamic: Anna Belardo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push her along, she should secure a comfortable lead from the gates and control the tempo entirely on her own terms on this Good Bath surface. Etienne and Polly The Sniper are the natural prominent types who will likely slot in just behind her, with Tree Wizard — a true prominent racer who has been remapped to midfield because the field holds more pace-seeking types than the shape can accommodate — likely unable to get its preferred early position. Our Fella and Cotai Jaunt will be racing from further back, making their runs late, but on a flat 5½f track at Bath where the rail can matter and the pace is likely to be measured rather than fierce, the advantage clearly lies with horses racing prominently — those who can travel just off the uncontested leader stand to benefit most from a race run to a fair but unfranticingly honest tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Anna Belardo Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Anna Belardo is allowed to stride clear from the front and set a measured, sustainable gallop unchallenged.
scenarios.body: She dictates from flag to finish on her own terms, conserving enough to repel any late challengers over the final furlong on the undulating Bath finish; her Good-ground form and front-running profile suit this shape precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Etienne or Polly The Sniper press Anna Belardo more assertively than expected and the pace quickens early.
scenarios.body: The resulting faster early fractions drain Anna Belardo's reserves approaching the final furlong, handing an advantage to the prominent horses who sat just behind the speed and travel well into the straight; Etienne's superior OR and recent form make her the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the front-runners empty inside the final furlong, allowing the closers to pick up ground rapidly.
scenarios.body: Our Fella's consistent placed form over this trip on Good ground and Cotai Jaunt's unknown ceiling give them each a theoretical route in, but Bath's 5½f layout rarely rewards horses who give the field a long start; this scenario needs everything to go right for the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Pace Muddles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at an unusually slow early tempo and the field concertinas, producing a messy finish with no runner fully exploiting their style.
scenarios.body: Tree Wizard, though racing out of its natural prominent role, could benefit from a bunched finish where positional style matters less; this is the least likely shape and depends on a chaotic tactical scenario rarely seen in small-field sprints.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Etienne or Polly The Sniper press Anna Belardo actively early — if they do, the pace lifts and Anna Belardo's stamina reserve becomes the key question over the final furlong.

Tree Wizard's jockey Abdulla Rashid Al-Hajri (5lb claimer) may attempt to push forward regardless; if Tree Wizard does force its way prominent it intensifies the pace battle and could compromise all the front-runners.

Our Fella's 2-day turnaround is unusually short and worth monitoring in the pre-race paddock — if the horse looks fresh and well it remains a genuine threat from hold-up for the places; if it looks jaded the recency is a red flag.

Cotai Jaunt for Ollie Sangster (3 wins from 30 runners in 14 days) is an unknown commodity whose ceiling is completely uncharted — Sean Bowen will know how much horse he has underneath him and could produce a surprise if the talent is there.

Bath's undulating straight rewards horses who meet the rising ground with momentum — prominent runners who travel into the final two furlongs on the bridle tend to hold on, so watch which horses are still travelling at the 2f pole.

races.name: Welsh Power 20th Anniversary Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier) (Div I)

runners_data.name: The Feminine Urge
runners_data.note: Redistributed to lead despite being a natural hold-up horse; Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) takes the ride for Grace Harris, who has sent out 6 winners from 25 in the last 14 days, and her Good-ground form figures read well (12 runs, 1W 4P), but racing from a wholly unnatural position means her chance hinges entirely on getting away cleanly and stealing a soft lead.

runners_data.name: Ten Club
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with a headgear flag and limited sim-going form (1W 2P from 5 runs), last seen 48 days ago and with a form string suggesting inconsistency (F, 7, 5); Finley Marsh rides and the trip drops to 5½f from recent 7f efforts, which may not suit a horse that needs time to warm into a race.

runners_data.name: Ken Brulee
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with the most encouraging recent form in the field — a win at 6f on Good and placed efforts at 5f and 6f on Good; Rob Hornby takes the ride and the horse carries a headgear flag (p), suggesting he needs to be switched on early, which on a comfortable tempo at Bath could see him travel well throughout.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old natural hold-up horse that the map places in midfield due to congestion at the rear; Alistair Rawlinson rides and the horse has a sim-going figure of 9/15 with 1W 3P, and recent placed form at 6f Good suggests he retains ability, though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.94) means his chance depends on a truly run race opening a gap.

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who ran just two days ago, which is a significant fitness flag; Taylor Fisher is in for Joe Tickle (0 wins from 7 in 14 days) and sim-going form is thin (0W 0P from 1 run), with a form string that has not shown anything at 6f+ — very hard to fancy here under this level of pressure and preparation.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Natural closer for Tony Carroll, who has placed 4 winners from 43 in the last 14 days, and the horse does have a win on Good at 6f in his recent history; however, last five runs show five losses with two 8th-place finishes, and the STYLE_FIT context means he needs a well-run race to get to the front — that race is unlikely to materialise here.

runners_data.name: Anglesey Lad
runners_data.note: Returning from 112 days off for Scott Dixon, who has sent out 0 winners from 19 in the last 14 days; placed form at 6f Good is there (2nd and 4th), and Kieran O'Neill rides, but the combination of a lengthy absence, no recent match fitness, and a trainer out of form makes this a speculative proposition despite his natural finishing ability.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Carries a headgear flag (p) and races for a trainer with only 0 wins from 5 in the last 14 days; Alice Bond's 5lb claim could be useful on a flat track, but the form string (-56580) and sim-going record (1W 1P from 9 runs) paints a horse who finds a way to be beaten, and being shuffled into a midfield role from her natural rear position compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with a visor (hg:v) for Kevin & Lauren Frost, back after 10 days; his recent form shows a 4th and 3rd at 7f Good before two blanks, suggesting he may want further than 5½f, and Olivia Haines' 7lb claim is the one mitigating factor, though he is another hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role that does not play to his strengths.

races.paceDynamic: The Feminine Urge is the lone identifiable pace-setter in this nine-runner 5½f handicap, redistributed to the front having been tagged as a true hold-up horse — meaning she will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop rather than a true front-runner's scorching tempo, and that artificial lead is unlikely to create genuine pressure. The field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types: Starsong, It's A Mugs Game, Port Hedland, Anglesey Lad, Rinky Tinky Tinky, and My Boy Jack are all natural closers pushed into midfield slots on the map because there is simply no room for them all at the rear, while Ken Brulee and Ten Club are also hold-up horses. Because the leader is not a natural front-runner and no horse is likely to force a true pace, this race is set to be run at a moderate, controlled tempo that will compress the field and produce a messy tactical affair with minimal separation until late. In a race where the pace is soft and artificial, hold-up horses attempting to close from off the pace face the worst outcome — the tempo is unlikely to string the field out, meaning positional advantage and race-reading mid-race will matter more than pure closing speed, and the horse who can travel smoothly and is most comfortable on Good ground at 5½f Bath, regardless of style tag, is best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Positional Win
scenarios.trigger: If The Feminine Urge sets an uncontested but comfortable tempo and the field fails to spread out, leaving the race to be decided by a late surge in a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop means closers get no real gap to fill, and the horse best positioned to track the pace and quicken off that tempo wins; Ken Brulee's recent Good-ground form and course-appropriate profile make him the archetype here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string the field fractionally and a true closer finds a gap late through the pack.
scenarios.body: A horse with genuine finishing speed on Good ground gets a clear run up the outside in the final furlong; Starsong's Good-ground sim record and Anglesey Lad's placed form at 6f on Good both suit this sliver of opportunity.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If The Feminine Urge, though not a natural front-runner, is allowed such an uncontested lead that she builds a cushion the closers cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: A race run truly to her own rhythm with no pressure could see her last home on Good ground; the STYLE_FIT discount applies, but the lack of any challenger for the lead means the scenario is not impossible despite her natural inclination to race off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Jostling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses scramble for the same late ground and produce a scrappy finish with a surprise winner from the wide draw or favourable position.
scenarios.body: With so many horses racing out of role and a compressed tempo, a lower-ranked horse gets a fortunate split or favourable position and edges the photo; Rinky Tinky Tinky or My Boy Jack could benefit from a fortunate passage in this shape.

watchPoints.text: The Feminine Urge is not a natural front-runner and if she misses the break or shows her true hold-up instincts in the first furlong, there will be no genuine pace in this race at all — monitor her stalls behaviour and early stride closely.

Ken Brulee's headgear flag (p) means he needs to be activated promptly; if Rob Hornby cannot get him into a flowing rhythm early on the sharp Bath track, his finishing effort could be blunted despite being the horse with the most relevant recent form.

It's A Mugs Game ran just two days ago — watch the market moves and paddock demeanour closely, as a horse racing on residual fatigue in a field this weak could still outrun a price but is a significant handling risk if she shows any sign of dullness.

Anglesey Lad returns from 112 days off — a horse coming back fresh for Scott Dixon (0/19 in 14 days) is a combination that demands respect for the possibility of a market move, but form students should treat his chance as conditional on him showing full fitness on the day.

With seven runners effectively redistributed out of their natural positions, watch the first two furlongs for positional jostling; any horse that stumbles into a clear-run midfield berth without expending early energy could emerge as the unexpected beneficiary of the compressed tempo.

runners_data.name: Honour Your Dreams
runners_data.note: Six-year-old on a retrieval mission after a poor last run, carrying the race's pace responsibility not by nature but by default — Michael Attwater's horse is genuinely a hold-up type pushed onto the front, so any free-running energy will drain her finishing reserves; tongue-tie noted, good going suits (7/15 in similar conditions).

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Joe Tickle who ran just two days ago — that turnaround is unusually quick and merits scrutiny, though his back-to-back third-place finishes on good and soft ground over 6f suggest he handles the surface; sits in pure hold-up territory by nature but the short break could compromise his peak output.

runners_data.name: Ten Cuidado
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partner who is genuinely a hold-up horse by inclination but the crowded rear forces him into a midfield role — his distance profile is all 7-8f on standard ground, making this 5½f trip on good turf a sharp ask; only one similar-going run from six attempts suggests ground form is thin.

runners_data.name: Cici's Secret
runners_data.note: Charlie Pike's three-year-old carries a clear finishing warning — a fader in her profile — and has run five times on good ground without winning or placing; her natural rear-running style is squeezed into midfield by the traffic, which compounds the finishing concern rather than alleviating it.

runners_data.name: Sisters In The Sky
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's seven-year-old has the most consistent recent form in the field (three top-four finishes in last four), and while she's a natural prominent/hold-up type crammed into midfield, her experience over 6f on good and firm allows her to travel efficiently wherever she settles.

runners_data.name: I Was Thinking
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's five-year-old last ran 33 days ago and has only one comparable good-going run from eight attempts in similar conditions — his nine-of-eleven last time out on firm was alarming, and the style compression into midfield means he cannot play to a closer's strengths here.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: William Carson rides this Tony Carroll six-year-old who was last seen finishing last of eight on good ground — a 10-day turnaround is brisk, and while he has placed on good and similar going, his prominent natural tendency is redistributed rearward, meaning Carson may have to settle further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Luke Morris on a three-year-old with the highest STYLE_FIT score of the redistributed group (0.93), suggesting he is closest to getting a natural position despite the map compression — his recent form string of 3-4-3-4-5 shows consistency just below the podium, and good ground suits (8/15 similar runs).

races.paceDynamic: Honour Your Dreams is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 5½f handicap, redistributed from her natural hold-up base to the lead because no other genuine pace-setter is present — she sets what should be a measured, uncontested gallop around Bath's sweeping track. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types: Ten Cuidado, Cici's Secret, Sisters In The Sky, I Was Thinking, Daley T, and Rogue Rebellion are all natural rear-runners compressed into midfield slots because they simply cannot all get to the back of a nine-runner field, meaning the pace map overstates how genuinely held-up this race will be. With Honour Your Dreams uncontested and setting a controlled tempo, the rail and the early positioning advantage matter enormously on this track, and runners who can travel prominently without being pushed to lead will be best placed. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit close behind the pace — true prominent/stalking types — rather than the cavalry of hold-up runners who will be fighting for ground from farther back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Honour Your Dreams dictates a sustainable solo gallop and the pack fails to close until too late.
scenarios.body: Honour Your Dreams sets an unforced pace through the first three furlongs, with any runner able to sit second or third on the rail tracking into a winning position off the bend; the genuine hold-up types trapped in midfield lack the acceleration burst to reel in those already in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the compression of hold-up types into midfield creates an unusually strong surge in the final furlong that overwhelms the front.
scenarios.body: Honour Your Dreams is caught in the final 100 yards as the bunched midfield group produces a wall of finishing power; runners with better recent form over this trip on good ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Honour Your Dreams goes off too quickly for her comfort zone and blows up entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A pacemaker tiring before the straight creates a vacuum that the trailing group rushes into, but this scenario is tempered by the fact that most closers here are redistributed and may not be sitting as far back as their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scrimmage No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling between the compressed midfield group disrupts rhythm and produces a messy, slow-burn result.
scenarios.body: With so many horses out of their natural positions, interference or traffic issues across the first two furlongs could randomise the outcome; runners on outside draws with clean air and proven course form are insulated from the trouble.

watchPoints.text: Honour Your Dreams will be racing entirely out of her natural style on the lead — watch in the first furlong whether Kieren Fox can settle her comfortably or whether she overcooks the pace, which would alter the entire race shape.

The six-runner compression into midfield from naturally rear-running horses means the first two furlongs could see significant jostling and positional fights — runners drawn wide (particularly Sisters In The Sky and Rogue Rebellion) may gain clean air while inner horses get squeezed.

Geemann's two-day turnaround after racing 48 hours ago is the sharpest fitness question in the field — if his energy levels are compromised, he may stop quickly in the final furlong despite looking well-placed early.

Bath's 5½f track rewards horses who settle just off the pace and move smoothly into the straight — the runner who secures second or third on the rail behind Honour Your Dreams without burning energy has a material positional advantage over the bunched midfield group.

Ten Cuidado and Daley T both have prominent-type headgear entries (hg:p) noted, meaning they may push forward earlier than their redistributed midfield slot suggests — this could create an unexpected secondary pace battle and tighten the race for those behind them.

runners_data.name: Call Time

runners_data.name: Stapleford Park

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer

races.paceDynamic: Wedgewood is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push him off his rhythm, should stride into a comfortable lead from the gates and control tempo throughout this 5f heat on Good ground at Bath. Call Time has prominent claims from a mapping perspective but is the only realistic challenger for early position, and even that match-up is unlikely to produce a genuine pace duel — Wedgewood should dictate unchallenged. The redistributed hold-up types — Coolagh Magic, Fancy Dancer, Jackie Brown, Symbol Of Hope, and Hi Hoh Tonto — are all genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, compressing the field and reducing the clean air and separation those horses need late. This race shape firmly favours a prominent or front-running profile: with Wedgewood able to control fractions, any horse that can travel close to him without burning fuel has a major positional advantage, while true closers are racing out of role and will struggle to generate their usual sustained late momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wedgewood Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wedgewood jumps cleanly and immediately asserts an uncontested lead, setting a measured but honest pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Wedgewood rolls along in front controlling every yard, and any horse with the tactical speed to sit close without over-racing inherits the best ground-saving position entering the final furlong. Call Time, travelling prominently just off the leader, is best placed to pounce if Wedgewood ties up, while Fancy Dancer — despite redistribution — has good 5f form and may get close enough to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Raider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Wedgewood's 72-day absence blunts his finishing effort and a prominent tracker swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Call Time, racing just off the pace, is the clearest beneficiary if the leader fades, with proven 5f form on Good ground and a freshish preparation giving cause for optimism. Fancy Dancer's placed 5f runs suggest she can sustain a finish when not buried too deep, and she is best of the redistributed group to make an impact if the scenario allows.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Snatch Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and the hold-up horses — forced up but still arriving late — manage to get the gaps they need.
scenarios.body: This is a structurally unlikely shape because the redistributed hold-up horses are racing out of their natural role, meaning their late kick will be dulled by the compromised position they are forced into early. Jackie Brown, with the best recent going-matching statistics of the group and proven form on Good turf, is the most likely of these to salvage a result if gaps materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scramble No Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break poorly, the field bunches, and the race devolves into a scrappy sprint with no clear pace narrative.
scenarios.body: In a compressed, shapeless race the tactical edge disappears and raw ability relative to the handicap mark becomes the deciding factor; Coolagh Magic's winning form on Good going is a marginal angle here. Mart, fresh off a 1-day turnaround and likely to find his own rhythm regardless, could outrun his odds if the field fails to sort itself cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Wedgewood's 72-day layoff is the single biggest swing factor — if he is ring-rusty at the start or lacks his peak fitness, the entire pace scenario collapses and Call Time inherits the lead without the unchallenged gallop that suits Wedgewood's profile.

Watch how many of the redistributed closers — Coolagh Magic, Fancy Dancer, Jackie Brown, Symbol Of Hope and Hi Hoh Tonto — actually attempt to race forward in the early stages; if several push up, a faster-than-expected early pace could compress the advantage Wedgewood is expected to enjoy.

Mart's one-day turnaround is the sharpest preparation in the field and trainer Donovan may have a specific reason to run him so quickly — monitor market movement, as a significant move would suggest this angle is sharper than the raw form implies.

Jackie Brown has the strongest going-match record among the hold-up contingent and Finley Marsh will be looking for any late gap; in a race where true closers are compromised, he is the one to keep onside if the pace scenario loosens in the final 100 yards.

Call Time arrives five days fresh for J S Moore fitted with headgear — the combination of race-readiness, 5f experience and a prominent profile maps neatly onto the likely race shape, making Taylor Fisher's positioning in the early stages worth noting at the start.

runners_data.name: Nora Barnacle
runners_data.note: Eighty-one days off the track for the Dominic Ffrench Davis yard is a significant fitness query; predominantly run over much shorter trips (1m-1m4f) with form on Soft or Standard rather than Good, making the combination of trip, going and layoff genuinely concerning.

runners_data.name: Notable Charm
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's three-year-old carries the lightest weight in the field and Rob Hornby is a quality booking; although placed recently on Good ground at 1m2f, the step to 1m6f is a significant stamina test for a horse whose best figures are at shorter, and its true hold-up style is shelved in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Lady Lauren
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles's juvenile filly is racing off the minimum weight and Gina Mangan takes the ride; a form string of -65065 offers little encouragement and the move to 1m6f from previous efforts at 1m-1m2f is an unproven stamina stretch for a horse yet to place on Good turf.

races.paceDynamic: Basilette is the one confirmed front-runner in this 1m6f contest and, with no genuine rival to press her early, she is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop that suits her stamina-based style over this longer trip. The field is heavily populated with hold-up horses — Trooper, Just Adair, Fram Castle, Prophet Squeeze, Cherry Cola, Alex The Great, Nora Barnacle, Notable Charm and Lady Lauren are all closers by nature, meaning the rear of the race will be congested and those at the back will need a strong pace to aim at, which Basilette is unlikely to generate alone. Several runners tagged as redistributed — notably Notable Charm, Prophet Squeeze and Cherry Cola — are genuine prominent or hold-up types who will not naturally slot into the midfield positions shown on the map; Basilette is the one horse virtually guaranteed to get her position. With one horse setting a steady, uncontested tempo over 1m6f on Good turf, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers or horses with a high cruising speed who can track Basilette closely and respond when the pace lifts in the straight, rather than deep closers waiting on a pace that may never truly develop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Basilette Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Basilette bowls along at her own pace with no rival willing or able to close her down early, allowing her to dictate margins throughout.
scenarios.body: Basilette has a strong recent record at this trip and going combination, and a solo, uncontested lead over 1m6f on Good ground can turn the race into a test of stamina and positioning rather than finishing speed. Horses who have tracked her closely — Just Adair and Fram Castle — are best placed to pounce, having the distance form and ability to respond off a moderate pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Basilette's solo lead is faster than it appears and genuine hold-up horses find clear runs in the straight to unleash finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: With ten runners and a field of closers bunched in the rear, any horse that finds a clear passage late could scythe through tiring rivals; Trooper and Just Adair carry distance form in this going and are best equipped to deliver late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed runner such as Notable Charm or Cherry Cola manages to secure a prominent position closer than their natural style and outstays rivals in a slowly-run race.
scenarios.body: A steady pace over a stiff 1m6f can stretch the field early enough for a horse travelling comfortably in second or third to simply outstay the field; however, the style-fit penalties on redistributed horses here reduce the probability that this scenario delivers cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a faster-than-expected early tempo from Basilette or an unexpected challenger causes the front to capitulate in the final two furlongs, handing the race to a true deep closer.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Basilette's confirmed solo front-running role and the absence of any rival likely to push her, but if she over-gallops, Trooper — a 1m6f+ specialist on Good ground — would be the primary beneficiary from the back of the field.

watchPoints.text: Basilette — if she strays off a true gallop in the opening half-mile with no rival to pressurise her, she could be almost impossible to catch over 1m6f on Good ground with her recent winning form at this trip.

Just Adair — Pat Cosgrave's booking for a horse stepping up from 1m2f to 1m6f for the first time deserves attention; if the trip is within her stamina range she has the placing form to go close, but a misjudgement in trip could see her fade late.

Notable Charm and Prophet Squeeze — both natural hold-up horses are mapped closer to the pace than they would naturally want; if either struggles to adapt to that position they may use up energy early and fail to produce their typical finish.

Nora Barnacle — an 81-day absence combined with an untested 1m6f trip and a shift to Good ground from her usual Soft/Standard surfaces means her readiness and suitability are both genuinely unknown today.

The congestion among true closers — Trooper, Cherry Cola, Alex The Great, Lady Lauren — means traffic and positional interference in the straight is a material risk; horses with the widest draw or best turn of foot from a clean position will have a significant edge.

races.name: Regal Gaming Grand Gallop Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sceptic
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping back to a mile for Ian Williams who has sent out 2 winners from 23 runners in 14 days; similar-going form is thin (0W1P from 4) and this far back in a big field, a clear run is far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's runner has won on Artificial and is at his best over a mile, but his last Good-ground form reads 0W1P from just 2 runs — a genuine hold-up type who will be hunting the same late ground as half this field, limiting his route to victory.

runners_data.name: Electric Bass
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters, likely to press Who Is Alice from the off; Roger Teal has been busy (4/12 in 14 days) and the stable is in form, though Electric Bass's last five runs suggest she tires at trip — a key watch for whether she can sustain the front-running effort over a mile.

runners_data.name: Thestral
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's juvenile hold-up type has placed over this course and distance on Good ground (3/8f/GOO), and Jack Doughty claiming is a useful weight advantage; wearing a hood, and the third-last run was a solid second at seven furlongs suggesting he can travel prominently enough in this shape.

runners_data.name: Galactic Glow
runners_data.note: Excellent recent Good-ground profile (10 runs, 1 win, 5 places) and Joe Tickle's yard is quiet in 14 days; a true hold-up horse working in a compressed rear group, meaning clean air is more luck than certainty — style-fit tempers enthusiasm despite the going credentials.

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride for David Evans (3/19 in 14 days) but this six-year-old is tagged as one who fades in the finish — over a mile on Good ground with a strongly run race, that fade flag is a significant concern in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Wildfell
runners_data.note: 405 days off the track is an enormous fitness question; last two runs on Good ground produced an eleventh and a seventh, and the form string of 79/00- offers little encouragement — William Carson's booking and a return to a mile barely offset the layoff concern.

runners_data.name: Havana Club
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's four-year-old won last time at eight furlongs on Firm, and the stable also runs Blue Hero — Finley Marsh rides and has current winning form over Good ground (3/8f/GOO, 1/8f/FIR); placed well enough in recent form but this is a hold-up runner who will need things to happen in front of him.

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old dual winner in recent form (1/10f/FIR, 1/8f/FIR), Joe Leavy rides for the same Wintle yard as Havana Club — his best form has come on Firm, and Good-ground figures show just 1W1P from four runs, so the surface is a mild step down from ideal conditions.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's booking for Ollie Sangster (3/30 in 14 days) stands out; a consistent prominent racer with a record of 2W6P from six Good-ground starts and all five recent runs over this or similar trips have produced a place — the profile fits the dominant scenario perfectly.

runners_data.name: Lovely Jubly

runners_data.name: Amathus

runners_data.name: Malakai Kite
runners_data.note: Unbeaten experience profile for a three-year-old whose style is unclassified; Luke Morris handles a horse with only four runs, all on Good or Soft, and the form reads 0W2P — a lightly raced type who could yet improve but the style uncertainty and inexperience are real risks at handicap mark 59.

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: One of the two front-runners tasked with setting the pace; Grace Harris has been striking at 6/25 in 14 days which is eye-catching, and the hood (h) is worn again — however, recent form reads five consecutive off-the-pace finishes, suggesting that early position is not always converted, making this a pace-dependent proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Who Is Alice and Electric Bass are the two confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field, and both are likely to press for the early lead from the jump, creating a genuinely contested gallop around Bath's sweeping mile. Good ground will ensure that pace is honest rather than suicidal, meaning the leaders will be asked questions from the outset but are unlikely to capitulate catastrophically. The weight of hold-up horses in this field is pronounced — Mbappe, Galactic Glow, Havana Club, Blue Hero, Lovely Jubly and Amathus are all true hold-up types redistributed toward midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded — meaning the genuine closers will be competing for the same late ground and cannot all deliver their ideal run. The race shape most favours prominent racers who can slot in just off the two leaders and produce a sustained challenge in the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who will face traffic and a lack of room; Buckland Belle is ideally positioned to exploit this shape. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can all get to the front-end in this shape, and of those who might push forward, Who Is Alice and Electric Bass are best placed to actually secure their positions, with Buckland Belle the most likely to anchor the prominent ground behind them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice and Electric Bass push hard for the front and set a genuine pace that strings out the field, rewarding the horse sitting third or fourth.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off on Bath's long run to the line, and a prominent tracker travelling powerfully just off the pace delivers the decisive move from two furlongs out. Buckland Belle, with her consistent Good-ground form and Tom Marquand aboard, is the prototype beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Last Standing
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Who Is Alice — is allowed to ease into a comfortable rhythm and the field fails to apply coordinated pressure.
scenarios.body: Who Is Alice controls proceedings without being challenged seriously in the early stages, converting the race into a test of stamina and rail-running rather than a sprint finish. Electric Bass, drawn to press, may fade, but the winner comes from the front third of the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge On Good Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, opening a broad late run for horses positioned in mid-division.
scenarios.body: Good ground at Bath can produce a flat finish when the front two tie each other up, and horses like Amathus and Galactic Glow — who have genuine Good-going form — could benefit from a well-timed challenge. However, the crowded hold-up group makes clean passages uncertain, and style-fit penalties apply to several of these runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Traffic, Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference, the pace is uneven and hold-up horses find gaps that would normally be closed.
scenarios.body: A messy renewal where jockeys lose position and a hold-up horse threads through late to claim an unlikely prize; Havana Club has winning form on Good ground and could capitalise if a gap materialises. This is the lowest-probability shape because the majority of true closers are racing out of role and face a structural disadvantage in this field.

watchPoints.text: Who Is Alice and Electric Bass are both confirmed front-runners — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which takes control and which is forced to concede the lead, as the winner of that early duel will shape the entire race.

Buckland Belle has been out just nine days after a recent run — watch for signs of any fatigue or freshness issues in the paddock, as Tom Marquand's tactical position off the pace depends on her travelling smoothly in the first half of the race.

Eagle Day carries a fade-in-finish flag and is ridden by Rob Hornby at the head of a prominent group — if he is allowed to coast in behind the leaders without being pressed, he could flatter before the final furlong, distorting the mid-race picture.

The hold-up cluster — Mbappe, Galactic Glow, Blue Hero, Havana Club and Amathus — will all be hunting the same inner ground in the final two furlongs; watch for potential traffic issues on the home turn as they converge and jockeys make decisions about where to switch.

Amathus wears a visor for the first time or in a notable context on his best-going profile — watch his early behaviour to assess whether the headgear sharpens him or provokes unwanted exuberance before settling into his hold-up role.

races.name: British EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Quebella
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer at his most patient, this hold-up filly likely trails the field early; her recent form (364-33) shows consistency without dominance, and 82 days off plus a step up to 1m3½f are questions, though Good ground suits and she needs the pace scenario to fully collapse.

runners_data.name: Pierian
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old boasts the strongest class in the field at OR 87 and a formidable Good-ground record (2W3P from five runs); she'll try to lead and if she can slip the other front-runners early, Marquand's positional intelligence gives her the best chance of any lead horse to last home over this trip.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jura
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's mare has the profile of a front-runner but her recent form (475253) shows she rarely wins from the front in competitive company; she has run 15 times on similar ground for one win, and at 47 days off and OR 79, the role she fills here is more likely as a pace-maker than a winner.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bird
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's consistent filly won over 10f on Good just 21 days ago and carries a prominent-racing style that maps perfectly to this race shape; she is 1W3P from six runs on similar going and Rob Hornby will look to sit a length off the front-running battle and pounce in the straight.

runners_data.name: Aravalli
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's lightly-raced three-year-old is in outstanding form — four wins from her last six, all on Good ground, including a recent 12f victory — and her prominent profile means she will travel economically just off the hot pace; Taylor Fisher rides and the stamina of the trip looks well within her compass based on her last two wins over 12f.

runners_data.name: Asset
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly carries confirmed front-running style and is in form (T14: 6/14), but her best efforts have come over 8-10f and the step to 1m3½f is unproven; Luke Morris will aim to lead but with Pierian and Spirit Of Jura contesting the same space, she may be forced to race prominently rather than lead, slightly compromising her preferred role.

races.paceDynamic: Pierian, Spirit Of Jura, and Asset all carry confirmed front-running profiles, guaranteeing a strongly contested early gallop over 1m3½f on Good ground at Bath — a track where the long home straight means pace advantage is rarely sustained without genuine stamina. With three horses competing for the same real estate from the break, the lead will be contested rather than gifted, meaning the pace will be honest but the front-runners will inevitably cost each other energy through the race. Prominent racer Mythical Bird and Aravalli sit just behind the brawl and are ideally placed to travel economically in the slipstream without burning early reserves. This race shape — a genuinely hot pace set by multiple front-runners burning each other off — strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield profile that can travel within the fractions, stay the trip on the extended mile-and-three-and-a-half, and produce a sustained finish rather than a sudden burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight a genuine battle for supremacy and the prominent pair travel economically behind them.
scenarios.body: Mythical Bird and Aravalli, sitting a length or two off the boiling pace, inherit maximum momentum at the home turn and sustain their runs up the straight as the front-runners capitulate; the Good ground and flat track suit a horse who can maintain stride rhythm rather than sprint sharply.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Pierian given class and Haggas/Marquand quality — establishes a clear lead quickly and the others are forced to concede the rail.
scenarios.body: Pierian has strong Good-ground form (2W3P in five runs on similar going) and the class edge at OR 87; if she makes clean use of her early speed and the others take each other on behind, she conserves enough to hold on through the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is truly scorching and all three front-runners visibly tie up inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Quebella, held up by Jamie Spencer in her customary patient style, would be the primary beneficiary as the field comes back to her; her stamina form at 10-12f on Good ground (sim-going 3/8, 0W2P) is modest but this is the scenario that most flatters her profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Lottery, All Change
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners eyeball each other into a slow early crawl before the pace suddenly explodes late, turning the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: This suits a horse with a high cruising speed that can accelerate sharply from a slow pace; Asset's best form is over shorter (8-10f) and she may have the turn-of-foot advantage in this unusual scenario, though the extended trip remains a question.

watchPoints.text: Aravalli arrives on the back of four wins from six runs on Good ground and her prominent profile slots directly into the most likely race shape — watch whether Taylor Fisher settles her cleanly off the hot pace.

Mythical Bird won 21 days ago and Hughie Morrison's horse has the form, the style, and the trip scope to capitalise if the three front-runners burn each other — Rob Hornby knows exactly where to be tactically in this scenario.

The battle between Pierian, Spirit Of Jura, and Asset for the lead in the first furlong is the race-defining moment — if one breaks sharply and the others concede immediately, Pierian could find herself in a lone leader scenario that dramatically changes the complexion of the race.

Spirit Of Jura's record of just one win from 15 runs on similar going suggests she functions as a pace-injector here rather than a genuine winner, but her presence ensures the gallop is honest throughout — monitor whether she stops abruptly in the straight.

Quebella has been off 82 days and Jamie Spencer will likely ride her last of all; she needs every other horse to tie up completely, and her 0 wins from 8 similar-going runs makes her a tail-risk rather than a primary threat.

runners_data.name: Douglas Dc

races.paceDynamic: Belle Amie is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Douglas Dc as a willing companion from the front, she should secure the lead with minimal fuss on Good ground at Bath over 1m3½f. The pace will be honest but controlled — Belle Amie has won from the front twice in her last five runs and Callum Shepherd will be able to dictate a rhythm that suits her stamina rather than her speed, making this a thorough staying test rather than a sprint finish. With no genuine pace duel to burn her off, she should bowl along comfortably through the first mile and ask serious questions of a hold-up field coming down the Bath hill. This race shape strongly favours the leader and any genuinely prominent types who can track within two lengths — closers who need a fast pace to generate momentum will find conditions less than ideal. The field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Trojan Truth and Offiah's Boy are both natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, and in a steadily-run race neither may get the sectionals they need to fire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Amie Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Amie bowls along at her own pace and the hold-up horses fail to generate sufficient momentum on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Belle Amie sets a fair but unhurried pace, Douglas Dc tracks her into the straight, and the closers find themselves too far back with too little pace to chase down a leader who has conserved energy throughout; Good ground and a flat finish at Bath rewards a horse who has already won twice at this trip on similar going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the middle mile to string out the field and give the genuine hold-up types a race to run at.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger gallop than expected opens up ground for Trojan Truth, who has three wins from ten outings on Good and is proven at 12f, to make significant late progress; Jodhpur Blue, placed three times from fifteen Good-ground starts, also has the profile to pick up ground if the tempo is right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Douglas Dc or a horse tracking the pace sits close enough to pounce when Belle Amie's effort flattens out in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Douglas Dc's trainer Tony Carroll has had four winners from 43 runners in the last 14 days showing strong current form, and an 8-year-old who has hit the frame six times from fifteen Good-ground runs knows how to find the line; if Belle Amie ties up late, a horse lobbing in second or third has first run on the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Open Finish, All Beaten
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses and the race turns into a dawdle followed by a sprint, shuffling the result unpredictably.
scenarios.body: A messy race with no genuine tempo sees a compressed finish in the straight where inexperienced judgement from the saddle or a traffic incident decides matters; in this scenario a lightly-weighted or fresh horse coming from an unexpected position could gate-crash.

watchPoints.text: Belle Amie's early stride pattern is critical — if Callum Shepherd gets a clean break and sets a relaxed rhythm, the hold-up field will struggle to close on Good ground at Bath.

Trojan Truth and Offiah's Boy are natural hold-up horses who will be racing further forward than ideal; watch whether they settle or get involved in unnecessary early position battles that drain their finishing reserves.
Douglas Dc's age (8) means he will strip fit after 15 days off with a yard in form, but watch whether he gets dragged into a contest too close to the pace too soon, burning his late run.
Jodhpur Blue carries a hood (hg:t) and his switching-off in the early stages will determine whether he has enough gas to deliver a late challenge — watch him through the first half mile.
The 5:02 race over the same 1m3½f trip on the same card will provide live sectional evidence of how the Going is playing and whether the straight is rewarding hold-up or prominent horses.
